text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Central Organization of Trade Union Organisations (SAK) representative backs Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto's argument that Environment Ministry's Natura 2000 programme should be reconsidered.
- Cooperative banking centre (OPK) and regional banks group agreed on a timetable to separate their operations.
- Finns' interest in travel abroad is picking up, sector says.
- It is very unlikely that British beef has been brought illegally to Finland, farm ministry says.
- Finnish customs confiscated 200,000 litres of contraband spirits on its way from China to Russia.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish paper industry should invest closer to European markets to cut transport costs, says professor of economics Eero Artto arguing Finnish forestry industry has lost its competitive edge.
- A merger between Neste and IVO would harm Finnish gas markets, says director of Nordic operations Jan-Erik Brask at Swedish power producer Vattenfall.
- Regional power company Espoon Sahko will join energy merger of Savon Voima and Kuopion Energia.
- Finnish lottery pays out 22 million markka on Saturday, money specialists advise wins should be invested in shares.
AAMULEHTI
- Talks of "romance" between Merita bank and insurer Sampo are unreal, caused by heatwave, says managing director Pertti Voutilainen at Merita.
- Young Finns consider newspapers as the most reliable, useful and informative media, a study by Suomen Gallup shows.
DEMARI
- Environment ministry's reputation damaged in the Natura 2000 debate, says chief secretary Olli Ojala at the ministry.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- With euro, new techonology and fierce competition, financial sector is facing a complete structural change, says director Heikki Koskenkyla at Bank of Finland's office of financial markets.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
